theme: China outbound and domestic travel data: CNTA/Ministry stats, Ctrip reports, Chinese holiday travel datasets, Hong Kong/Macau arrivals
queries_run: gh search repos: china tourism statistics
gh search repos: hong kong visitor arrivals
gh search repos: macau visitor arrivals
gh search repos: china tourism data
gh search repos: china holiday travel
WebFetch github.com/search: hong kong visitor arrivals
WebFetch github.com/search: chunyun spring festival travel
WebFetch github.com/search: china tourism academy OR CNTA statistics

candidates.name: china-tourism-dataset
candidates.what_it_holds: Single committed CSV `china_tourism_2015_2023.csv` (12.6KB), 31 Chinese provinces/regions x 9 years (2015-2023): columns year, province, domestic_tourists_mln, inbound_tourists_mln, tourism_revenue_billion, gdp_billion, population_mln. E.g. Beijing 2015: domestic 199.75mn, inbound 9.168mn, tourism revenue RMB190.63bn. Appears compiled from official (NBS/provincial statistical yearbook) tourism figures; no source citation or code, just the flat file. No commit history/stars visible beyond the single file; unclear licence.
candidates.why_useful: Directly addresses gap #7 (regional travel volume outside US/EU, China domestic+inbound) with province-level granularity and a longer 9-year run; could be cross-checked/extended for a China domestic-travel base rate, though ABNB's China exposure is minor so relevance is mostly as a macro-context comparator, not a KPI driver.

candidates.name: _baiduqianxi_ (Baidu Migration Platform API client)
candidates.what_it_holds: Python client (87 stars, updated ~13 days ago per search snapshot) for Baidu Qianxi ("Baidu Migration"/慧眼) — China's near-real-time population-flow index built from Baidu Maps location data, giving city-to-city and intra-city movement intensity indices, historically used by researchers/media to track Chunyun (Spring Festival travel rush) and holiday travel surges since ~2015.
candidates.why_useful: Baidu Qianxi is the closest thing to a real-time China domestic-travel-intensity proxy (used academically for COVID mobility and holiday-travel studies); a pull method for it would let the team build a China domestic travel-intensity index analogous to TSA throughput, addressing gap #7/#20-style mobility proxies, though it requires validating against any China revenue-relevant KPI (currently unclear if worth building given ABNB's small China footprint).

candidates.name: baidu_qx
candidates.what_it_holds: Python scraper (13 stars, last updated June 2023) for Baidu migration data at city/province/country granularity — alternative/older client for the same Baidu Qianxi mobility index as _baiduqianxi_ above.
candidates.why_useful: Secondary/backup implementation of the Baidu migration-index pull; useful if the primary client repo goes stale, same rationale as above (China domestic mobility proxy).
candidates.time_coverage: through mid-2023 (repo activity), index itself ongoing

candidates.name: bd_qianxiCrawler
candidates.what_it_holds: Python crawler (10 stars, updated April 2024) collecting Baidu migration city-level flow indices plus inbound/outbound movement and commuting metrics — a third independent client for the same underlying Baidu Qianxi source, more recently maintained than the two above.
candidates.why_useful: Most recently active of the three Baidu-migration clients found; same China domestic-mobility-proxy rationale, worth noting as the freshest fallback method.

candidates.name: Web-crawlers-travel-information
candidates.what_it_holds: Python web crawlers (2 stars) extracting travel information from three Chinese OTA platforms: Ctrip (携程), Tuniu (途牛), and Qunar (去哪儿) — no committed dataset, method only.
candidates.why_useful: A scraper template for Chinese OTA listing/price/route pages could, if run (a ToS decision for a human per repo rules), proxy Chinese domestic/outbound travel search intensity or route pricing; flagged as method only, not run.

candidates.name: Tourist-Flow-Web-Crawler
candidates.what_it_holds: Python crawler (2 stars) built to support academic research on spatial patterns of tourism flow in the Chengdu-Chongqing region of China, likely pulling from a Chinese OTA/review site (description suggests Ctrip-adjacent).
candidates.why_useful: Regional (sub-national) Chinese tourism-flow research tooling; could be adapted to other Chinese metro regions for a domestic-travel-flow proxy, low current usefulness given narrow regional scope and low maintenance.

candidates.name: ftcr_outbound_tourism
candidates.what_it_holds: Financial Times interactive-graphics scaffold (public-archive, JS/bower/CircleCI build, last updated Oct 2017) for a "2017 China Outbound Tourism report" published article; repo contents inspected are build tooling (.bowerrc, .editorconfig, .circleci) rather than a raw data file — any underlying dataset is likely embedded in build assets or sourced externally (e.g. CNTA/UNWTO/CLIA figures cited in the FT piece) rather than committed as a clean CSV.
candidates.why_useful: Points to an FT-sourced compilation of 2017-vintage China outbound tourism statistics (likely CNTA/CTA figures); low direct usefulness since it is an archived news-graphics repo, not a data repo, but the FT article's underlying numbers (if extractable) could seed a historical outbound-tourism baseline.

candidates.name: outbound_tourism_china
candidates.what_it_holds: Small HTML repo (1 star, last updated 2018) titled around China outbound tourism; not inspected in depth (budget-limited) beyond search metadata — likely a student/coursework data-visualization project rather than a primary dataset.
candidates.why_useful: Possible small compiled dataset on China outbound tourism trends; low confidence given age (2018) and lack of direct file inspection, flagged for completeness only.

candidates.name: Market-Reports-on-China
candidates.what_it_holds: Repo (0 stars, last updated Feb 2019) described as analysis covering the market situation and future outlook for Chinese tourism traveling abroad, 2019-2025 period — likely a report/slide compilation rather than raw structured data; not inspected further given very low signal (0 stars, single description line, stale).
candidates.why_useful: Possible secondary-source outbound-tourism market outlook narrative for China 2019-2025, marginal value as it's likely qualitative/report-style rather than a dataset.

notes: This theme is thin on GitHub relative to others we have scouted: no repo was found holding official CNTA (China National Tourism Administration / Ministry of Culture and Tourism) monthly/quarterly statistics as structured data, no Ctrip investor/quarterly-report data extraction repo, and zero hits for Hong Kong Tourism Board or Macau DSEC visitor-arrival series (searches for 'hong kong visitor arrivals', 'macau visitor statistics', 'Macau DSEC tourism', and 'data.gov.hk tourism' all returned 0-2 irrelevant repos). The strongest finds were three independent Python clients/scrapers for the Baidu Qianxi ('Baidu Migration') population-mobility index, which is the closest proxy on GitHub for China domestic travel-intensity/holiday-rush (chunyun) tracking, and one small province-level China tourism CSV (2015-2023, domestic+inbound+revenue by province) that plausibly extends our regional-travel-volume gap (#7) though only as a low-frequency annual series. Given ABNB's minimal direct China revenue exposure, this theme's ceiling for KPI-forecasting value looks low regardless of what exists on GitHub -- the bigger blocker is that official CNTA/HKTB/DSEC arrivals data is published as PDFs/web tables on government sites, not as GitHub-hosted datasets, so a scraper of those official sites (not attempted here, and would need a human ToS call per repo rules since they're outside the sanctioned-source list) would likely beat anything catalogued here. WebSearch quota was exhausted mid-task (hit the session's 200-call budget from other concurrent scouts); all post-quota discovery was done via WebFetch against github.com/search HTML, which worked but hit transient 429s requiring one 45s backoff-and-retry. gh search repos hard limit (6 calls) was reached early and not exceeded; gh api contents was used 3 times (well under the 8-call cap).
